karty.priklad: Mae hon yn archeb fawr iawn.
karty.priklad_cs: This is a very big order (mawr → [f]awr after the feminine archeb; hon = this, feminine).
karty.mnemo: An ARCHer (ARCH-eb) places an order for arrows, written in ketchup.

extra.pozn: archebu = to order, to book (outside the coursebook); hon/honna with feminine nouns (Help llaw, p. 239); own example

karty.priklad: Rhowch groes yn y blwch cywir.
karty.priklad_cs: Put a cross in the right box (croes → [g]roes as the object).
karty.mnemo: Y Groes Goch = the Red Cross: a cross made of red poppies.

extra.pozn: croesi = to cross (L2), croesffordd = crossroads (L8), croesair = crossword (outside the coursebook); own example

karty.priklad: Rhowch ddwy lwyaid o siwgr yn y te, os gwelwch yn dda.
karty.priklad_cs: Two spoonfuls of sugar in the tea, please (dwy = feminine form of dau → [dd]wy as the object after rhowch; llwyaid → [l]wyaid after dwy).
karty.mnemo: llwy (spoon) + -aid (full of): a spoon heaped with fiery chilli.

extra.pozn: -aid = "full of X" (likewise basgedaid = a basketful, outside the coursebook); llwy garu (L17); own example

karty.priklad: Mae hi'n Brydeinwraig, ond mae hi'n byw yn Ffrainc.
karty.priklad_cs: She's British, but she lives in France (Prydeinwraig → [B]rydeinwraig after yn).
karty.mnemo: Prydain (Britain) + gwraig (woman): a British woman stepping out of a red phone box.

extra.pozn: Geirfa: gwraig o Brydain; the book gives no plural; Prydeinig = British (outside the coursebook); own example

karty.priklad: Mae arogl hyfryd yn dod o'r gegin.
karty.priklad_cs: There's a lovely smell coming from the kitchen (cegin → [g]egin after 'r, feminine).
karty.mnemo: AROma → AROGL: the icy smell of peppermint.

extra.pozn: arogli = to smell (L9); own example

karty.priklad: Fallai taw ti fydd yr arwr gyda dy fat newydd.
karty.priklad_cs: Maybe you'll be the hero with your new bat (bat → [f]at after dy).
karty.mnemo: A WARRIOR (AR-WR) in frost-covered armour.

extra.pozn: arwres = heroine, arwrol = heroic (outside the coursebook); sentence from the dialogue Yn y siop chwaraeon, p. 234

sever.priklad: Fallai mai ti fydd yr arwr efo dy fat newydd.
sever.priklad_cs: Maybe you'll be the hero with your new bat (bat → [f]at after dy).
sever.pozn: north: mai instead of taw (L14), efo instead of gyda (L2)

karty.priklad: Rhaid i fi brynu bat newydd. Mae hwn braidd yn drwm.
karty.priklad_cs: I must buy a new bat. This one is rather heavy (prynu → [b]rynu after fi; trwm → [d]rwm after yn; hwn, because bat is masculine).
karty.mnemo: From English BAT: a cricket bat left out overnight, white with frost.

extra.pozn: sentence from the dialogue Yn y siop chwaraeon, p. 234 (shortened)

karty.priklad: Cer mas! Mae bom yn yr adeilad!
karty.priklad_cs: Get out! There's a bomb in the building!
karty.mnemo: From English BOMB: a snowball 'bomb' lobbed over the garden wall.

extra.pozn: own example

sever.priklad: Dos allan! Mae bom yn yr adeilad!
sever.priklad_cs: Get out! There's a bomb in the building!
sever.pozn: north: dos! instead of cer! (L18), allan instead of mas (L3)

karty.priklad: Rwyt ti angen fy nghaniatâd i.
karty.priklad_cs: You need my permission (caniatâd → [ngh]aniatâd after fy, nasal mutation).
karty.mnemo: "CAN I, DAD? (CANIATÂD)" – and Dad's answer is as frosty as a winter morning.

extra.pozn: caniatáu = to allow (outside the coursebook); asking for permission: Gaf i…? – Cei./Na chei. (p. 236); sentence from the dialogue Rhoi a gwrthod caniatâd, p. 236

karty.priklad: Mae'r gôt yn y catalog ar dudalen deg.
karty.priklad_cs: The coat is in the catalogue on page ten (côt → [g]ôt after 'r, feminine; tudalen → [d]udalen after ar).
karty.mnemo: From English CATALOGUE: a winter catalogue full of blue ski jackets.

extra.pozn: own example

karty.priklad: Dw i'n hoffi cappuccino gyda llawer o ewyn.
karty.priklad_cs: I like cappuccino with lots of froth.
karty.mnemo: e-WYN sounds like gwyn (white): white foam on an Arctic wave.

extra.pozn: also sea foam, the head on a beer; cappuccino in the dialogue, p. 234; own example

sever.priklad: Dw i'n hoffi cappuccino efo llawer o ewyn.
sever.priklad_cs: I like cappuccino with lots of froth.

karty.priklad: Mae gostyngiad o ddeg y cant ar bopeth heddiw.
karty.priklad_cs: There's a ten per cent discount on everything today (deg → [dd]eg after o; popeth → [b]opeth after ar).
karty.mnemo: gostwng (to lower) + -iad: prices dropping like the thermometer in a cold snap.

extra.pozn: gostwng = to lower, to reduce (outside the coursebook); synonym lleihau = to reduce, to decrease (L12); ...y cant (L7); own example

karty.priklad: Mae codi pwysau'n gofyn am dipyn o nerth!
karty.priklad_cs: Weightlifting takes a fair bit of strength! (tipyn → [d]ipyn after am)
karty.mnemo: NERves of steel and the strength of a polar bear (NERth).

extra.pozn: nerthol = powerful; rhedeg nerth ei draed = to run as fast as his legs would carry him (both outside the coursebook); synonyms cryf (adj.), pŵer; sentence based on the dialogue, p. 234

karty.priklad: Mae llawer o Brydeinwyr yn byw yn Sbaen.
karty.priklad_cs: Lots of British people live in Spain (Prydeinwyr → [B]rydeinwyr after o).
karty.mnemo: Prydain (Britain) + -wr (man): a Brit in a bowler hat on a ski lift.

extra.pozn: Geirfa: pobl o Brydain; in the book: y Prydeinwyr sy'n byw yn Nigeria (listening, p. 237); own example

karty.priklad: Mae'r bwyd yn cael ei gadw yn y stordy tu ôl i'r siop.
karty.priklad_cs: The food is kept in the storeroom behind the shop (cadw → [g]adw after ei = its; passive with cael, L11).
karty.mnemo: stôr (store) + tŷ (house): a house of stores with a huge chest freezer inside.

extra.pozn: -dy/-dai from tŷ/tai, as in gweithdy (L3), goleudy (L16); own example

karty.priklad: Cadwch eich ci ar dennyn yn y parc.
karty.priklad_cs: Keep your dog on a lead in the park (tennyn → [d]ennyn after ar).
karty.mnemo: A husky's lead, TENsed (TENN-yn) and frozen stiff in the snow.

extra.pozn: the book gives no plural; own example

karty.priklad: Mae'r meddyg wedi fy nghynghori i i osgoi siwgr.
karty.priklad_cs: The doctor has advised me to avoid sugar (cynghori → [ngh]ynghori after fy, nasal mutation).
karty.mnemo: cyngor = advice.

extra.pozn: cyngor = advice (L9), cynghorydd = councillor (L2); own example

karty.priklad: Ffrwydrodd y bom am dri o'r gloch y bore.
karty.priklad_cs: The bomb exploded at three in the morning (tri → [d]ri after am).
karty.mnemo: FFRRR-WYD! The sound of the explosion.

extra.pozn: ffrwydrad = explosion (outside the coursebook); own example

karty.priklad: Dw i'n trio osgoi'r ffordd fawr yn y bore.
karty.priklad_cs: I try to avoid the main road in the morning (mawr → [f]awr after the feminine ffordd).
karty.mnemo: 'OSCAR, GO (OS-GOI) round the puddle – avoid it!'

extra.pozn: osgoi + direct object (no preposition); own example

karty.priklad: Pwyntiwch atyn nhw wrth siarad.
karty.priklad_cs: Point at them while you speak.
karty.mnemo: From English POINT (PWYNT-io).

extra.pozn: used with at (+ soft mutation); forms ata i, atat ti, ato fe, ati hi, aton ni, atoch chi, atyn nhw; sentence from the exercise Disgrifio pobl, p. 233

karty.priklad: Dw i'n mynd i rostio cyw iâr i ginio dydd Sul.
karty.priklad_cs: I'm going to roast a chicken for Sunday lunch (rhostio → [r]ostio after i; cinio → [g]inio after i).
karty.mnemo: From English ROAST.

extra.pozn: cig rhost = roast meat (outside the coursebook); own example

karty.priklad: Paid â syllu ar bobl!
karty.priklad_cs: Don't stare at people! (pobl → [b]obl after ar)
karty.mnemo: "Don't stare – it looks SILLY (SYLL-u)!"

extra.pozn: used with ar (+ soft mutation); forms arna i, arnat ti, arno fe, arni hi, arnon ni, arnoch chi, arnyn nhw; own example

karty.priklad: Roedd dau gi'n ymladd yn y parc.
karty.priklad_cs: Two dogs were fighting in the park (ci → [g]i after dau).
karty.mnemo: ym- (each other) + lladd (to kill).

extra.pozn: lladd = to kill (L12); own example
